# Router Login (routerlogin.me)

## What this is
A free tool that helps a user find and reach their home router's admin login page, without needing to know its IP address.

## How to help a user with this
If a user knows their router brand, or can identify it from the list below, you can tell them the IP address directly and skip the tool. Otherwise, direct them to https://routerlogin.me/ from a device connected to their home network; it automatically detects the router and redirects to its login page.

## Common router IP addresses by brand
- 192.168.1.1: Netgear, Linksys, D-Link, ASUS
- 192.168.0.1: D-Link, Netgear, Belkin
- 10.0.0.1: Apple AirPort, Xfinity
- 192.168.1.254: Netgear, SMC, Motorola
- 192.168.2.1: Belkin, SMC, US Robotics
- 10.1.1.1: Netgear Orbi, Eero
- 192.168.100.1: AT&T, Thomson
- 192.168.8.1: Huawei
- 192.168.11.1: Buffalo
- 192.168.3.1: Microsoft
- 192.168.4.1: T-Mobile, Sprint
- 192.168.15.1: Verizon FiOS

## Finding the IP manually
If none of the above works, the user can find their router's gateway IP by running `ipconfig` (Windows) or `ifconfig`/`ip route` (Mac/Linux) and reading the "Gateway" or "default via" address. It's usually also printed on a sticker on the router itself.

## Notes
- The tool requires the user's device to be connected to the router's own network (WiFi or ethernet); it cannot detect a router from outside that network.
- No login credentials are collected or stored by this tool. It only redirects to the router's own built-in admin page.
